cover.title: 5 niche ways to find the european chatgpt visitors your analytics hides

inner.title: check the direct bucket
inner.body: terminus says most assistant traffic arrives with no referrer, so it lands in direct, and chatgpt mobile apps almost never send one. your newest channel may be filed under a name you ignore.

inner.title: build the assistant channel
inner.body: ga4's ai assistant channel covers chatgpt, gemini, deepseek, copilot and grok, but not claude or perplexity. those two stay in referral until you add a custom channel group above it.

inner.title: count the consent gap
inner.body: when a visitor denies analytics_storage, ga4 sets no cookies and sends cookieless pings for modeling. modeling needs 1,000 events a day with consent denied for 7 days, so a small site may get none.

inner.title: read the server log
inner.body: openai names two agents: oai-searchbot surfaces sites in chatgpt search, and chatgpt-user opens a page when someone asks a question. count both in your server log, because a tag built for browsers will never list them.

inner.title: filter the utm tag
inner.body: terminus says chatgpt on desktop web appends utm_source=chatgpt.com to citation links, so you can filter it. app clicks carry nothing, so treat that number as a floor, not the total.
